label: Bible Study
prompt: Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too _____ for thee:
verse: Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee:
note: Jeremiah prays this while buying a field in a city about to fall — faith with a deed attached.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new _____ and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.
verse: Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.
note: Peter looks forward to new heavens and a new earth where righteousness is finally at home.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and _____ them beneath the mount.
verse: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.
note: The KJV says 'brake' — Moses saw the calf and dancing and shattered the tablets at the mountain's foot.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep, eating flesh, and drinking wine: let us eat and drink; for to _____ we shall die.
verse: And behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep, eating flesh, and drinking wine: let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.
note: Jerusalem partied under siege; Paul quotes this line in 1 Corinthians 15.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which _____ not.
verse: Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.
note: 'The law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not' — the legal trap that sent Daniel to the lions' den.
